extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and environmental advocates submitting public comments on agency rulemakings and NEPA reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting effective public comments to agencies (particularly NEPA reviews and regulatory rulemakings), emphasizing specificity, evidence, originality, and strategic submission tactics to maximize agency attention and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify what you're responding to and clearly state what changes you want. Reference particular sections or paragraphs of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to exact provisions, sections, or paragraphs and say precisely how they should be changed (what language to add/remove or what decision to make). Specificity makes it easier for agency staff to locate and respond to the point you're raising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Support your argument with quantitative information, studies, citations, and analysis of applicable laws or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include credible studies, statistics, citations, legal analysis, or other quantitative evidence to back claims. Data and citations increase credibility and give agencies a factual basis for responding or adopting your recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Original / Personalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in your own words to explain why the issue matters to you personally, rather than relying solely on form letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe personal impacts, local observations, or unique perspectives. Original, personalized comments are more likely to be treated as distinct and to resonate with reviewers than identical form letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Submissions Count More Than Bundled Files
rubrics_metrics.description: If you deliver comments as one big bundled file they are treated as a single submission; individual emails/comments are counted separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting many people’s comments as a single file if the intent is to have each counted separately. Organize so each person’s comment is a discrete submission to increase the apparent number of individual commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical Letters Carry Weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical letters carry weight because of the time investment required to write them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sending mailed letters in addition to electronic submissions; agencies may perceive physical letters as reflecting greater effort and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customize Form Letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Customize form letters by selecting resonant points and rewriting in your own words — this takes only minutes longer but makes a significant difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t send unedited form letters. Edit to include local details, change wording, and emphasize 1–2 points most relevant to you so the comment reads as distinct and substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix Submission Methods and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary submission methods and timing to maintain agency attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple channels (email, agency web portals, mailed letters) and stagger submissions so comments do not all arrive at once. Diverse methods and timing can help sustain agency staff awareness of the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA-Specific Mechanics: Agencies Must Address Each Distinct Issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Under NEPA, agencies responding to comments must address each distinct issue raised. One letter covering five different issues requires five separate responses, while 100 identical comments require just one response to that single issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because agencies must respond to distinct issues, submitting original comments that raise multiple, specific concerns increases the agency’s response burden and the chance your issue is addressed; by contrast, identical/form comments are operationally less demanding for agencies to reply to.
